entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 758 of 2023
Revisionist :- Delinquent Child (Changed Name Shyam Sunder) Thru. Mother Smt. Shobhawati
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt. Lucknow And 3 Others

Counsel for Revisionist :- Gulam Rabbani
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Subhash Vidyarthi,J.
1.

Heard Sri Gulam Rabbani, the learned counsel appearing for the revisionist, Sri Anant Pratap
Singh, the learned Additional Government Advocate and perused the record.

2. By means of the instant revision filed under Section 102 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, the revisionist has challenged the validity of the orders dated 06.02.2023 passed by the Juvenile Justice Board, Faizabad rejecting his application for release on bail and the order dated 01.05.2023 passed by the Child Court, Faizabad/ Ayodhya dismissing Criminal Appeal No. 12 of 2023 filed by the revisionist against the order rejecting his bail application.
3.The opposite party no. 2 lodged an FIR 409 of 2021 on 23.09.2021 alleging that the revisionist had enticed away the complainant's daughter aged about 15 years on 14.09.2021.
Delinquent Child (Changed Name Shyam ... vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173014682/
1 4.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In the statement of the victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., she stated that she loves the revisionist and wants to marry him but as her family members were not agreeing for it, she had gone away with the revisionist.

A similar statement was given by the victim before the Magistrate while getting her statement recorded uner Sectino 161 Cr.P.C. and she categorically stated that no misdeed had been committed against her.
5. Social Enquiry Report submitted by District Probation Officer does not contain any such recommendation as would justify continuance of his custody.
6. Keeping in view the aforesaid recommendations of the District Probationary Officer, I am of the view that the revision deserves to be allowed.

The orders dated 06.02.2023 passed by the Juvenile Justice Board, Faizabad and the order dated 01.05.2023 passed by the Child Court, Faizabad/
Ayodhya, are set aside.
8. Let the revisionist-Juvenile be released on bail in Case Crime No. 409 of 2021, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC & Sections 3/4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012,
Police Station Raunahi, District Ayodhya upon his guardian furnishing a personal bond with two solvent sureties of his relatives, each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Juvenile Justice Board concerned subject to the following conditions:-
(i) the natural guardian will furnish an undertaking that upon release on bail the juvenile will not be permitted to come into contact or association with any known criminal or allowed to be exposed to any moral, physical or psychological danger and further that the guardian will ensure that the juvenile will not indulge in any criminal activity;
(ii) natural guardian will further furnish an undertaking to the effect that the juvenile will pursue his study at the appropriate level which he would be encouraged to do.
(iii) juvenile accompanied by his natural guardian, will report to the Probation Officer on the first working day of every calendar month.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The D.P.O. shall maintain a diary recording their attendance.

(iv) The District Probation Officer will keep strict vigil on the activities of the juvenile and regularly draw up his social investigation report that would be submitted to the Juvenile Justice Board concerned.
9.

It is made clear that the observations made in this order are limited to the purpose of determination of this bail application and will in no way be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
The trial court/J.J.Board shall be absolutely free to arrive at its independent conclusions on the basis of evidence led, uninfluenced by any finding or observation whatsoever in this order.
